The patient was treated. The national platform accepted the claim. Then the insurer refused to pay.

How a hospital gets paid

Treated. ✓
Submitted. ✓
Rejected.

In Saudi Arabia and the UAE, every insured visit becomes an electronic claim. The hospital sends it through a national platform (NPHIES in Saudi Arabia, DHPO and Shafafiya in the UAE) to the patient's insurer, who decides whether to pay. Too often, the answer is no.

Saudi Arabia · first submission

15–25%

of insurance claims are rejected
the first time they are sent.

The care was already given. Each rejected claim must now be found, fixed and resent by hand, or the hospital is never paid.

SAR 5–8 bn

rejected at first pass, every year.

100 claims. 20 come back.

KPMG, via Eye of Riyadh · SAR 5–8 bn = ~SAR 33 bn of health claims paid in 2024 (ME Insurance Review) × 15–25%; assumes the rate holds by value as well as by count.

Not one hospital

It happens across
the whole system.

Healthcare in Saudi Arabia and the UAE runs on insurance. Every insured visit creates a claim, so the leak repeats millions of times a year.

14.5 m

people with health insurance in Saudi Arabia.

SAR 18.5 bn

in health premiums. In one quarter.

Insurance Authority, Q1 2026. Every insured visit becomes a claim, in Saudi Arabia (NPHIES) and the UAE (DHPO, Shafafiya).

Why claims come back

The doctor wrote
for care.
Not for the insurer.

Doctors write notes to treat the patient. Insurers want specific proof that a test was necessary. When that proof is missing, the claim is rejected, even though the care was right.

40.5%

of denials in one Saudi study: medical necessity not justified.

Clinic note · Orthopaedics
Pt c/o lower back pain.
Exam: tenderness L4–L5.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine.
What the insurer needs to see
✕ How long the pain has lasted
✕ Treatment already tried
✓ Diagnosis code
40.5% of 13,974 claims, Saudi study as summarised by Noqta (secondary source, to be confirmed). More than 80 denial codes are in use.

The gap after the platform

The platform checks the format.
Not whether the insurer will pay.

NPHIES and DHPO check that a claim is filled in correctly. They don't check whether the insurer will accept it. So a claim can pass the platform and still be rejected weeks later.

“Medical necessity not justified.” Back to the billing team.
NPHIES validates messages; it does not decide whether an insurer will pay. A high technical acceptance rate can sit alongside heavy insurer rejection (Noqta).

Dubai rules · Nov 2025 directive

Two tries to fix it.
Then the money is gone.

When a claim is rejected, the billing team has a fixed number of chances and days to correct and resend it. In Dubai, that's two resubmissions. After the last one, the hospital can't recover the money.

written off every year in Saudi Arabia, after every retry.

Al Tamimi on the DHIC claims directive (effective 16 Nov 2025); Abu Dhabi: resubmit within 45 days of remittance (DoH). Write-off: Klystron estimate, assumes 50–70% of rejected value is recovered.

Why it happens

  • Notes don't justify medical necessity
  • Rules differ by payer and emirate, and change
  • Platforms check format, not payment
  • Denial data is thrown away, so nothing learns

Who feels it

  • Billing teams, reworking files for weeks
  • Doctors, called about patients seen long ago
  • CFOs, with cash months late or never

What it costs

  • SAR 5–8 bn rejected at first pass a year
  • SAR 1.5–4 bn never recovered
  • Recovered cash still arrives 1–4 months late

What's missing: a check against what the insurer will pay, before the claim leaves, and a clock on every denial after.

What ClaimReady does

Three jobs, one product.

Each job removes one of the causes we just saw. Together they mean fewer claims rejected the first time, and no rejection lost to the clock.

1

Check before sending

Every claim is checked against each insurer's rules and against this hospital's own past rejections. Risky claims are held, with the exact fix shown.

Fixes: rules that differ by insurer
2

Ask the doctor

When the note is missing what the insurer needs, the doctor gets one short question to confirm or edit. The AI never writes in the medical record.

Fixes: notes written for care, not insurers
3

Recover the rest

Every claim that still comes back lands in one queue, sorted by deadline and value, with the reply already drafted.

Fixes: short deadlines, lost denial data

Where AI is used

AI flags and asks.
It never codes.

AI is used only where fixed rules can't do the job. It never assigns medical codes or changes a claim. A person always decides.

15.2%

GPT-4's agreement with human coders on inpatient codes. Too low to let AI code.

📈

Risk score

Learns which claims this hospital's payers reject. Low confidence goes to review, never auto-block.

Target: ≥50% of holds truly needed a fix
📝

Documentation check

Reads the note in Arabic and English. Drafts one question for the doctor. Never adds a clinical fact.

Target: ≥80% of flags accepted by coders
↩︎

Denial reader

Sorts free-text denial reasons and drafts the reply. A biller always edits and sends.

Target: ≥90% agreement with billers

No AI for eligibility, format checks, prices, deadlines or the audit log. Those are fixed rules.

Appl Clin Inform 2025 (GPT-4, 15.2%); npj Health Systems 2025 (fine-tuned models, 69% exact match). Accuracy targets are measured in shadow mode before anything is held.

Q&A · Objections

What hospitals will say, and our answer

“Patient data can't leave our network.”It never leaves the country. Read-only, masked before any AI step, on-premise if needed.
“We already have Waseel / our system.”Keep them. They send the claim; we make sure it's worth sending, and work it when it comes back.
“No budget this year.”SAR 75k pilot, credited in full, with a written exit. Break-even is 1% of what's already rejected.
“IT will take months.”A read-only database view or nightly file. We do the work; IT grants access.
“We don't trust AI with claims.”Neither do we. It never changes a claim or code. It flags, explains and asks; a human decides.
“Who supports us in Arabic?”A named Riyadh/Dubai implementation lead, Arabic interface, support SLA in the contract.
“You're new to healthcare.”Fair. You see results on your own data before paying for a year. Source-code escrow and data-export rights.
